There is just one change to the team following last weekend’s big win over the Knights in Newcastle.
Josh Feledy comes into the starting side to replace injured centre Tolu Koula (ankle). Koula will miss the remainder of the regular season after suffering a moderate grade syndesmosis injury against Newcastle.
Feledy, a local junior, bagged a 16-minute hat-trick of tries against the Knights after replacing Koula late in the first half. They were his first three tries for Manly.

'I set myself that goal': Caleb's Bati dream alive after fairytale comeback
Six months ago, Caleb Navale thought his Rugby League World Cup dream was over.
A ruptured ACL during Manly's pre-season left the the 23-year-old lock fearing he would miss the biggest moment of his career so far, representing Fiji on the game's ultimate stage.
Now, after defying the odds with a remarkable return to the NRL just six months and three days after the training mishap, Navale has put himself firmly back in the frame for this year's World Cup.
“I set myself that goal when I was watching the last World Cup,” Navale told NRL.com.
“I was pretty devastated at the time, thinking I'd miss out on it.”
Caleb Navale Try
Instead, his comeback has felt like something out of a movie.
After months of rehabilitation, Navale returned in Round 25 against Newcastle, helping Manly snap a six-game losing streak and capping the afternoon with a try in his first game back.
“It was like a fairytale game for myself,” he said. “I'd been thinking about it for a while when it happened in pre-season.
"Just how it unfolded, coming off six losses, Saturday afternoon, scoring a try in my comeback game ... it was awesome.”
The comeback has reignited a dream that started long before he reached the NRL.
Watching the Rugby League World Cup as a young fan, Navale promised himself he would get there one day.
“Watching it when I was younger, I always dreamt of playing in one,” he said.
“It's becoming a reality very soon, which is amazing.
“Seeing all the boys like Tui (Kamikamica) and (Viliame) Kikau, and seeing how much it means to them coming from that little island in the middle of the Pacific, it's hard to put into words how much it means to my family and everyone.”

It's not the journey but the destination that counts now: Turbo
Tom Trbojevic’s return has come at exactly the right time for Manly, with the Sea Eagles skipper back on deck as they prepare for the two biggest games of their season.
After helping his team snap a six-game losing streak with a win over the Knights, Trbojevic has given the Sea Eagles renewed belief heading into the final two rounds, even if their top-eight hopes hang by a thread.
The first part of the assignment is Friday's clash with the Dragons at 4 Pines Park before travelling to Auckland in Round 27 to face the Warriors.
The ninth-placed Sea Eagles know they must win both games and then rely on results elsewhere to sneak into the top eight. Otherwise it's no finals for a second year running.
“All we can control is these two games of footy,” Trbojevic said.
“Unfortunately, we have put ourselves in this situation and it’s disappointing considering where we were.
Knights v Sea Eagles – Round 25, 2026
“Ultimately, we have two games of footy left and we need to win both.”
The 29-year-old pulled up well from his first game back after a hamstring injury, playing a key role in Manly’s 44-24 win over the Knights.
“Pulled up good,” Trbojevic said.
“It was good to get back out there and get the two points.”
His return has provided a timely boost for a Sea Eagles side that looked destined for finals oblivion after six losses in a row between Round 18 and 24.
Good to be back: Tom Trbojevic with wife Kristi after his comeback game in Newcastle. ©Shane Myers
Manly had enjoyed a promising start under Kieran Foran, but a mounting injury toll to key players disrupted their momentum.
Now, with their captain back and just two games remaining, Trbojevic believes there is still plenty of good footy to play.
“When we are at our best, we are a really good footy side,” he said.
“There’s been periods this year that we have been so far away from that. There’s too big a gap from our best and our worst.
“Overall this year we are really growing as a side.
“Two games to go to continue to do that and, if the stars align, we’ll see where we are at.”
The Sea Eagles also received another boost against Newcastle, with Josh Feledy making the most of his opportunity after replacing the injured Tolu Koula.
Feledy finds the line
The young centre scored a hat-trick and could be the attacking difference Manly has needed, as he prepares to line up in the starting side against the Dragons.
“Foz has really simplified it: prepare like you are going to play,” Feledy said.
“We need to go out there with a good mindset and we need to win both games, and that’s what we’re going to do.”

Manly’s 44-24 upset of Newcastle was exactly the response they needed after six consecutive defeats had threatened to completely bury their season. The Sea Eagles arrived at McDonald Jones Stadium as outsiders against a Knights side pushing for a top 4 finish, yet played with far more energy and intent than they had shown throughout their slump.
The biggest difference was Tom Trbojevic. Returning from his hamstring injury, Turbo ran for 154 metres and immediately gave Manly a more dangerous attacking shape. Josh Feledy scored the first try of his career, which turned into a hat-trick, while Lehi Hopoate produced nine tackle breaks and 151 metres and Reuben Garrick added 156 metres. The outside backs completely overwhelmed Newcastle in yardage and gave Manly the platform they had lacked during their losing run.
That performance was a reminder that this roster still has plenty of attacking upside when its best players are available. Turbo’s support play completely changes the way Manly can attack around the middle, while Jason Saab, Garrick and Hopoate provide speed and finishing on the edges.
The issue remains whether one good performance can be trusted after such a poor month. Manly lost six straight before the Newcastle win, repeatedly conceding soft points and failing to close games they had opportunities to win.
Tolu Koula’s ankle injury is another blow this week, although Feledy’s form last Saturday makes the positional reshuffle easier to absorb. Manly still have Jamal Fogarty controlling territory, Haumole Olakau’atu giving them an elite right edge weapon and Jake Trbojevic providing experience through the middle.
Most importantly, they are back at 4 Pines Park. Their finals equation requires them to win both remaining games and hope other results fall their way. It is a long shot, but it is still something to play for.

items.body_excerpt:
St George Illawarra Dragons have confirmed dummy half Jacob Liddle has been ruled out for the rest of the season with a calf strain.
When Liddle went down in the first half of their Round 25 clash with the Canterbury Bulldogs there were fears he had injured his Achilles.
When speaking with Dragons media, head of performance Dan Lawson revealed the club was initially concerned by the severity of the injury, saying, “It looked pretty bad, we were quite concerned to start off with.”
In an X (formerly known as Twitter) post, Nrl Physio revealed that the non-contact mechanism when pushing up off the line to then turning around to "see who kicked me" motion pointed towards an Achilles injury.
Liddle missed the start of the Dragons' 2026 campaign after suffering a high-grade hamstring injury during pre-season training in January.
The Dragons began the season without any dummy half back-up as reserve grade regular Connor Muhleisen was in rehab for an ACL injury he suffered during the 2025 Knock-On Effect NSW Cup Grand Final.
Connor Muhleisen in action. (Photo: Flickr- @NAPARAZZI)
After making his first appearance for 2026 off the bench in Round 3, Liddle was set to make his first start in Round 7 after a late change by Coach Shane Flanagan at the time.
However, he re-aggravated his hamstring injury in the warm-up which would send him for another stint on the sidelines.
The club have provided an update on the injury with Dan Lawson stating that "the scans were positive, he has a calf strain, not as bad as previously thought."
With the Dragons out of contention for the finals series and the nature of the injury with a three-week turnaround, Liddle won't play for the Red V again in 2026.
Liddle will now set his sights on a strong pre-season where he aims to retain the starting hooking position that he won late on this year with Damien Cook departing the club for the Castleford Tigers on a 2-year-deal at season's end.

Cook will return to the starting role this week as the Dragons take on the Manly Sea Eagles , with Muhleisen being recalled to first grade for the first time since Round 27, 2024 in the no.14 position.

As it happened: Bulldogs punish Dragons; Wahs roll on; Manly stun Knights
Three enormous matches with top-eight consequences light up a sensational Saturday of NRL action with Manly kicking off the day with a stunning 44-24 upset over the Knights.
After six losses on the trot the Sea Eagles were desperate to hit back and they did it in style with Tom Trbojevic running for 154m in his comeback match and Josh Feledy grabbing his first career hat-trick.
The win keeps Manly's faint finals hopes alive and leaves the Knights in danger of missing the top four and the double chance.
The Warriors then piled on a big score to rack up their 16th win of the season and join the Panthers and Roosters on 38 competition points as the race for the minor premiership goes down to the wire.
The final score at Accor Stadium was 45-26 as props Mitch Barnett and James Fisher-Harris both grabbed tries and Taine Tuaupiki had a night out with the boot as he nailed eight from eight.
That field goal from Luke Hanson also propelled the Warriors to top of table at least until tomorrow night .... by one point on for and against.
We wind down our Saturday triple with the Dragons and Bulldogs squaring off at Allianz Stadium.
Having put together back-to-back wins for the first time in a year the Dragons were playing with new-found confidence and would have loved to take a slice of revenge for a heartbreaking golden point loss to the Bulldogs in the season opener in Vegas.
However, they made far too many errors and could not execute their attack - whereas the Bulldogs were able to make their plays stick.
Racing to a 24-0 lead by the break, the Bulldogs were able to withstand a show of resistance in the second half from the Dragons to get the important win.
